text.tspan: Amazon CloudFront: a CDN that caches your content at the edge
PUT, POST, PATCH, OPTIONS, DELETE and dynamic requests skip the REC
and go from the POP straight to the origin (they are not cached).
TTL: how long a file stays cached
Default 24 hours (86,400 s) · minimum 0 s · no maximum.
After the TTL, the edge asks the origin again.
Course: "cached for a TTL (maybe a day)".
If you change the origin, CloudFront doesn't know until the TTL
Course: "hundreds of Points of Presence (edge locations, caches)"
• Improves READ performance: content is cached at the edge, close to users → better user experience, less load on the origin.
• Works for static content (images, video, JS/CSS, downloads) AND dynamic content (APIs, whole sites, WebSocket) over HTTP/HTTPS.
• DDoS protection because it is worldwide: attacks are absorbed at hundreds of edge locations, with Shield and WAF integration.
